findings.subject: all-contracts
findings.summary: Only 3 of 76 contracts declare the component `intent` block, and the schema does not require intent, states or slots, so completeness is unchecked.
findings.evidence: Only button.json, badge.json and input.json have `intent` (docs/design-system/cross-renderer-contracts.md:46 says so); component-intent.schema.json top-level `required` is only component/maturity/contract (+lists), `intent`, `description`, `states`, `slots` optional. 53/76 contracts have no `description`; 32 of those also have no crossRenderer.intent, so 32 contracts state no purpose at all (e.g. tooltip, popover, sheet, menu, kbd, spinner).
findings.fix: Make intent (at minimum a one-line purpose plus the platform-neutral axes) required in the schema, and require `states` and `slots` lists (allowing an explicit empty list with a description for static components). Backfill the 73 contracts.

verified.reason: Reproduced: only button/badge/input have `intent`, the schema's oneOf requires only component/maturity/contract, and 33 contracts carry no description or crossRenderer.intent. But the `intent` block is by design a cross-renderer semantic-axis map (cross-renderer-contracts.md:44-56), not a purpose field, so it is not expected on every contract. Purpose is published elsewhere: agent-index has e.g. tooltip summary "Tooltip supplies brief supplementary text...". 73/76 contracts list states, and the 3 without (alert, app-view, separator) are plausibly stateless. The real gap is that purpose and completeness are not enforced in the contract layer, which is a quality gap and does not block ready.

findings.subject: all-contracts
findings.summary: State names drift across contracts in ways the consistency lint does not catch: focus vs focus-visible, rest vs default vs idle, hover vs hovering, pressed vs active.
findings.evidence: `focus` is the listed state in input.json:11, textarea.json:7, breadcrumb.json:7, item.json:25, search-field.json:6, toggle-group.json:10 and toggle.json:8 while 21 contracts use `focus-visible` and AGENTS.md rule 11 forbids :focus rings (input only papers over it with stateAliases focus->focus-visible, input.json:155; textarea/search-field crossRenderer.requiredStates also say `focus`, textarea.json:48, search-field.json:38). Resting state is `rest` in 29 contracts but `default` in field.json:8, form.json:7, frame.json:22 and `idle` in feedback-state.json:17, load-more-trigger.json:7, resizable.json:8, scroll-area.json:8, scrollable-list.json:8. scroll-area uses `hovering` (19 others `hover`). `active` means current/selected in input-otp, navigation-menu, sidebar-nav-tree while button/toggle use `pressed`. `node scripts/design-system/check-contract-consistency.mjs` -> "Contract consistency OK (76 contracts)" with none of these in contract-consistency-baseline.json.
findings.fix: Add these synonyms to lib/contract-consistency.mjs (focus->focus-visible where the recipe draws :focus-visible, default/idle->rest, hovering->hover), baseline them, then rename in contracts with stateAliases for one release.

verified.reason: Reproduced from source. input/textarea/breadcrumb/item/search-field/toggle-group/toggle list `focus` while about 21 contracts use `focus-visible`, and accordion/button use `focusVisible`. Resting state is `default` in field/form/frame and `idle` in resizable/scroll-area/scrollable-list/feedback-state, against `rest` elsewhere and `resting` in badge. scroll-area uses `hovering`. input-otp and navigation-menu use `active`. `node scripts/design-system/check-contract-consistency.mjs` prints "Contract consistency OK (76 contracts)." Only input has a stateAliases entry. Mitigation: `focus` on text fields behaves like :focus-visible. Even so, this is exactly the C2 near-synonym class the lint misses.

findings.subject: all-contracts
findings.summary: Of the 31 cross-renderer contracts only Button and Badge map their axes to iOS; the other 29 map states only, and conformance tests check states and outcomes, never axes.
findings.evidence: Only button.json and badge.json carry intent.platforms.ios axis maps; input.json maps only size md. dialog sizes, toggle sizes/tones, segmented-control sizes/variants/tones, slider/progress tones, tabs sizes, avatar sizes/shapes, card variants, item variants/sizes/tones, toaster tones, carousel dot axes have no iOS mapping. packages/ui-react/src/conformance/renderer-conformance.ts:3-9 records implementedStates and outcomes only. Where iOS axes are checked they are hard-coded literals, not read from the contract: packages/ui-ios/Tests/Atom63UITests/AtomVariantParityTests.swift:11-12 (`AtomFieldVariant == ["default","filled"]`, `AtomCardVariant == ["default","filled","elevated"]`).
findings.fix: Extend the `intent.platforms` map (props -> axes, with extensions) to every crossRenderer contract, generate the Swift enums from it as for Button/Badge, and make the generator fail when a web axis value is neither mapped nor an extension.

verified.reason: Reproduced. Only badge.json, button.json and input.json contain an `ios` platform block, and input's maps only minHitTarget. renderer-conformance.ts:3-9 records implementedStates and outcomes, with no axes. AtomVariantParityTests.swift:11-12 hard-codes `["default","filled"]` and `["default","filled","elevated"]` instead of reading the contract. iOS counterparts with axes exist (AtomCard, AtomAvatar, AtomToggle, AtomProgressView, AtomToast, AtomPageDots), and no documented decision defers their mapping.

findings.subject: all-contracts
findings.summary: Maturity is self-declared: 69 of 76 contracts say `stable` with no check tying it to a scorecard, and the docs catalog defaults a contract-less component to Stable.
findings.evidence: 69 stable / 7 preview (amount, app-view, chat-composer, chat-message, chat-steps, chat-typing-indicator, message). apps/docs/src/lib/component-catalog.ts:742 `status: getComponentMaturity(slug) ?? 'stable'`. Stable components still carry open craft debt: docs/design-system/audits/craft-baseline.json:4,13-19 (kbd mode-branch and token-role; alert, card, input-otp, kbd, progress, slider token-role). No script reads maturity against any readiness file.
findings.fix: Default unknown maturity to `preview` (or fail), and add a check that `stable` requires a ready scorecard in docs/design-system/audits/readiness/ once layer 3 lands; demote components whose scorecard is not ready.

verified.reason: The counts (69 stable / 7 preview) and the `?? 'stable'` default at component-catalog.ts:742 are real. But the bar itself lists the C5 check as "— (cross-checked against layer 3)", so having no automated maturity script is not a gap against the bar. The craft-baseline debt cited is minor token-role and mode-branch entries, which do not show a stable component is unready. The only concrete dishonest-maturity case is progressive-blur, which contracts-11 already covers. As a cross-cutting claim it is unproven without the layer-3 scorecards.

findings.subject: all-contracts
findings.summary: The new consistency lint covers too little: it applies the size synonym only to a list literally named `sizes`, skips every object-form list, and knows two synonyms.
findings.evidence: scripts/design-system/lib/contract-consistency.mjs:23-26 (SYNONYMS has only sizes.default->md and resting->rest), :41 (`!Array.isArray(values)` skips valuesList/concat lists such as badge semanticVariants/solidVariants, input variants, frame variants, carousel dotTones), :45 (`SYNONYMS[list]` so sidebar.json:11 `menuButtonSizes: ["default","sm","lg"]` is not flagged). No rule compares list key names (sides vs directions, aligns vs alignments) or tone values (accent vs primary vs default).
findings.fix: Match size synonyms on any key ending in `Sizes`/`sizes`, resolve object-form lists through `values`/`concat`, add a list-name synonym rule and a tone-value rule, then re-baseline.

findings.subject: all-contracts

findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/progressive-blur has tsx/stories/test and an agent-index entry with `contract: null`; packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/menu.json has no component, no test and no index entry (`pnpm -s atom63 component menu` -> `No component "menu". (component.not_found)`). Both pass check:agent-index and check:contracts (sweep/summary.tsv exit 0).
findings.fix: Add to check:agent-index (or check:contracts) a bidirectional set comparison: every ui-react component directory has a contract and every component contract has a component or is moved to contracts/shared.

findings.subject: progressive-blur
findings.summary: ProgressiveBlur is an exported, documented component with no contract at all, so its axes (ProgressiveBlurPosition), defaults, slots and states are nowhere in the contract layer.
findings.evidence: No packages/ui-foundation/contracts/components/progressive-blur.json; packages/ui-react/src/components/progressive-blur/{progressive-blur.tsx,stories,test} exist; `pnpm -s atom63 component progressive-blur` prints "Status: Stable" and "TypeScript remains the source of truth for complete prop contracts" with no axes; agent-index.json entry has `contract: null`.
findings.fix: Write contracts/components/progressive-blur.json (positions axis, default, slots, states, maturity preview until scored), run generate:contracts and generate:index.

verified.reason: Reproduced. There is no contracts/components/progressive-blur.json, while ui-react/src/components/progressive-blur/{tsx,stories,test} exist. In agent-index.json it is the only one of 76 entries with `contract: null` and `axisGuidance: null`, and it exports ProgressiveBlurPosition. A missing contract meets P0 = missing. No documented exemption found; production-readiness-audit.md:78 only notes its missing recipe.

verified.reason: Reproduced: agent-index publishes progressive-blur with contract null, and no check rejects it (it is the sole null). This is a C4 wiring gap. It largely overlaps contracts-9 but is a distinct check failure.

findings.subject: progressive-blur

findings.fix: Give it an explicit maturity in its new contract (preview until its layer-3 scorecard is ready) and remove the stable default (contracts-4).

verified.reason: Reproduced: component-catalog.ts:742 `getComponentMaturity(slug) ?? 'stable'`, and agent-index lists the status as stable. ui-react-stable-action-matrix.md:50 itself marks progressive-blur P0 "Do not promise stable compatibility until an owner... evidence are recorded", so Stable is dishonest.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: Badge `accent` and `neutral` mean different things on web and iOS inside the same contract.
findings.evidence: Web: badge.json:16 `accent` is a solid-variant extension "A neutral on the control hover surface" (intent.platforms.web extensions, ~:153); `neutral` is a palette hue (badge.json:43). iOS: intent.platforms.ios.props.tone.map (badge.json:241) maps `accent` -> tone primary, emphasis solid and `neutral` -> neutral soft; generated AtomBadgeTone (packages/ui-ios/Sources/Atom63UI/Generated/AtomComponentIntent.generated.swift:5-11) exposes `.accent`. A port of `<Badge variant="accent">` to `AtomBadge(tone: .accent)` changes neutral to brand solid.
findings.fix: Rename the iOS case to `primary` (deprecated alias `accent`) to match the intent tone axis, or rename the web extension; keep one meaning per name.

verified.reason: Reproduced. In badge.json, web `accent` is a variant extension described as "A neutral on the control hover surface" (around line 153), and `neutral` is a hue-group extension (line 224). The iOS tone map (around line 237) maps `accent` to primary/solid and `neutral` to neutral/soft. The generated AtomBadgeTone exposes `.accent`. Same name, different meaning within one contract: a C2 violation and a porting hazard.

findings.subject: badge
findings.summary: Badge crossRenderer.requiredStates are checked against the web variant list, where `neutral` and `accent` happen to exist as a palette hue and an extension, so the requirement is satisfied by the wrong values.
findings.evidence: badge.json:281 requiredStates ["neutral","accent","success","warning","error"] with foundationAxis `variants`; scripts/generate-cross-renderer-contracts.mjs:90-95 only checks membership in that concatenated list (solid+semantic+palette).
findings.fix: Check requiredStates for badge against intent.axes.tone instead of the raw variant list, and use `primary` for the shared tone.

findings.subject: amount
findings.summary: Amount has an iOS counterpart (AtomAmountText) that mirrors its `fractions` axis, but amount is not a cross-renderer contract and maps nothing.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-ios/Sources/Atom63UI/AtomAmountText.swift:6-12 ("Mirrors the amount contract's fractions axis"), Tests/Atom63UITests/AtomAmountTextTests.swift; amount.json has no crossRenderer; cross-renderer.json components list (31 entries) omits amount.
findings.fix: Add amount to cross-renderer.json with a crossRenderer block and an intent map for sizes and fractions; generate AtomAmountFraction from it.

verified.reason: Reproduced. AtomAmountText.swift:6-7 says "Mirrors the amount contract's `fractions` axis". amount.json has only $schema/component/contract/lists/maturity keys, with no crossRenderer or intent, and cross-renderer.json has 31 components and omits amount. Under C3 a web contract with an iOS counterpart must map its axes. Amount being preview does not remove the ready-blocking gap.

findings.subject: menu
findings.summary: The `menu` contract is a shared recipe with no component, no test and no CLI entry, yet sits among component contracts.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/menu has only menu.css and menu.stories.tsx (stories comment: "Static preview of the shared .a63-Menu-* recipe"); `pnpm -s atom63 component menu` -> not_found.
findings.fix: Move it to contracts/shared (or a recipe contract kind) without maturity, and make the consumers (dropdown-menu, context-menu, menubar, select) reference it.

findings.subject: menu
findings.summary: The menu recipe contract omits states its own story draws: checked and destructive items.
findings.evidence: menu.json:8 states [rest, highlighted, disabled, selected, submenu-open]; apps/storybook/visual/__screenshots__/ui-react-menu-tones-chromium-linux.png shows "Checkbox (checked)" and "Delete"/"Delete (highlighted)" destructive rows; dropdown-menu.json and context-menu.json list checked/unchecked/destructive.
findings.fix: Add checked, unchecked and destructive to menu.json states so the shared recipe and its consumers agree.

findings.subject: menu
findings.summary: Menu names its highlight tone `primary` where every other contract names the same cue `accent`.
findings.evidence: menu.json:6 tones ["neutral","primary"]; tones elsewhere: item, progress, segmented-control, sidebar-nav-tree, slider, table, toggle use ["neutral","accent"]; AGENTS.md rule 5 tells builders to set `tone="accent"` on a selection. Screenshot ui-react-menu-tones-chromium-linux.png labels it "primary (data-tone)".
findings.fix: Rename to `accent` with a one-release alias.

findings.subject: menu
findings.summary: `stable` on a recipe-only contract claims a readiness nothing can score: there is no component, test or docs page for it.
findings.evidence: menu.json maturity stable; no menu.tsx/menu.test.tsx; not in agent-index.
findings.fix: Drop maturity when it moves to contracts/shared (contracts-15).

findings.subject: select
findings.summary: Select lists no `invalid` or `hover` state, and its recipe draws neither invalid nor documents hover, though Field puts it in an invalid state.
findings.evidence: select.json:7 states [closed, open, placeholder, focus-visible, disabled, highlighted-item, selected-item, disabled-item]; grep of select.css finds :hover but no data-invalid/aria-invalid selector; field.json:8 lists invalid; input.json and textarea.json list invalid.
findings.fix: Add invalid (and hover) to the contract; the layer-3 batch 3 reviewer should verify the trigger draws the danger edge.

findings.subject: checkbox
findings.summary: Checkbox omits hover and focus-visible though its recipe styles both and Radio lists focus-visible.
findings.evidence: checkbox.json:8 states [unchecked, checked, indeterminate, disabled, invalid]; checkbox.css has :hover and :focus-visible selectors; radio.json lists focus-visible.
findings.fix: Add hover and focus-visible to checkbox states.

findings.subject: toggle
findings.summary: Toggle's state list mixes two models (on/off and rest/pressed) and names `focus` where the recipe draws `:focus-visible`, so `pressed` is ambiguous between "on" and "being pressed".
findings.evidence: toggle.json:8 states [off, on, rest, hover, pressed, disabled, focus]; toggle.css uses [data-pressed] (the Base UI on state, 5 selectors) and :active, and draws the ring at toggle.css:132 `.a63-Toggle:focus-visible`.
findings.fix: States: off, on, hover, active (or pressing), focus-visible, disabled; document that data-pressed = on.

findings.subject: toggle-group
findings.summary: ToggleGroup takes `size` and `tone` props that its contract does not declare.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/toggle-group/toggle-group.tsx:30-31 (`size?: ToggleSize`, `tone?: ToggleTone`) and :54-56 (data-size, data-tone); toggle-group.json lists variants, orientations, selectionModes, states, slots, tokenSlots only. button-group.json does declare sizes for the same pattern.
findings.fix: Add sizes and tones (referencing Toggle's lists) with defaults to toggle-group.json.

findings.subject: frame
findings.summary: Frame's `states` list holds axis values, and two axes have no default.
findings.evidence: frame.json:22 states [default, border-off, border-subtle, border-strong] duplicates the `borders` axis [off, subtle, strong]; `trays` and `panelSurfaces` lists have no defaultTray/defaultPanelSurface in contract.
findings.fix: Remove the border values from states (Frame is static: states may be empty with a reason) and add defaults for trays and panelSurfaces.

findings.subject: toaster
findings.summary: Toaster's `tones` list includes `loading`, which is a state, and has no default tone.
findings.evidence: toaster.json:9 tones [default, info, success, warning, error, loading]; contract has defaultVariant only; states (toaster.json:8) lack loading.
findings.fix: Move loading to states, add defaultTone.

findings.subject: toaster
findings.summary: Toaster names its neutral tone `default`; every other tone list uses `neutral`.
findings.evidence: toaster.json:9 vs tones in button, item, menu, progress, segmented-control, sidebar-nav-tree, slider, table, toggle (all `neutral`).
findings.fix: Rename to `neutral` with an alias.

findings.subject: sidebar
findings.summary: One contract uses two size scales: menu buttons use `default`, sub-buttons use `md`; the lint misses it because the key is not `sizes`.
findings.evidence: sidebar.json:11 menuButtonSizes ["default","sm","lg"], defaultMenuButtonSize "default"; menuSubButtonSizes ["sm","md"], default "md"; sidebar.sides left/right is already in contract-consistency-baseline.json.
findings.fix: Rename menuButtonSizes default -> md; extend the lint (contracts-5).

findings.subject: drawer
findings.summary: The same concept (which edge an overlay attaches to) is `directions` in Drawer and `sides` in Sheet and Tooltip, and `directions` also means incoming/outgoing in Message.
findings.evidence: drawer.json:6 directions [top,bottom,left,right]; sheet.json:6 sides [right,left,top,bottom]; tooltip.json:6 sides; message.json:7 directions [incoming,outgoing].
findings.fix: Rename Drawer's axis to `sides` (alias `direction`), and keep `direction` only for Message.

findings.subject: connected-panel
findings.summary: ConnectedPanel has a `variant` prop (`button-group` | `default`) that its contract does not declare.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/connected-panel/connected-panel.tsx:77 `export type ConnectedPanelVariant = 'button-group' | 'default'`, :89, :162 data-variant; connected-panel.json lists aligns, slots, states, visualArchetypes only. A baseline exists for it: ui-react-connectedpanel-button-*.png.
findings.fix: Add variants and defaultVariant to connected-panel.json and type the prop from the generated list.

findings.subject: connected-panel
findings.summary: Alignment is `aligns` here and `alignments` in Tooltip.
findings.evidence: connected-panel.json:7 aligns [start,center,end]; tooltip.json:7 alignments [start,center,end]; input.json:58 group aligns.
findings.fix: Pick one key (`aligns`, used twice) and rename tooltip's with an alias.

findings.subject: context-menu
findings.summary: ContextMenu items take a `variant` (`default` | `destructive`) typed inline, not from the contract; DropdownMenu declares the same axis as itemVariants.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/context-menu/context-menu.tsx:127 `variant?: 'default' | 'destructive'`; context-menu.json has slots, states, visualArchetypes only; dropdown-menu.json has itemVariants + defaultItemVariant.
findings.fix: Add itemVariants/defaultItemVariant to context-menu.json (or reference the shared menu list).

findings.subject: field
findings.summary: Field's recipe styles an `outline` FieldGroup variant that no contract or prop declares.
findings.evidence: packages/ui-react/src/components/field/field.css:60 `.a63-FieldGroup[data-variant='outline']`; field.tsx declares only FieldLegendVariant (legend|label); field.json has no group variants.
findings.fix: Either declare a FieldGroup variants list or delete the dead selector.

findings.subject: button
findings.summary: Button uses `tone` for two different value sets: the prop list is neutral/muted while the intent axis is neutral/muted/primary/destructive.
findings.evidence: button.json lists.tones ["neutral","muted"] vs intent.axes.tone ["neutral","muted","primary","destructive"]; the CLI shows axis `tones` values [neutral, muted] (agent-index button contract.axes). A builder reading the intent will pass tone="primary", which the prop rejects.
findings.fix: Rename the prop-level list to something like `quietness` or document in the intent that primary/destructive tone is reached only through `variant`; keep one value set per name.
